description: A database provisioning spec declares a fully validated PostgreSQL instance definition — platform, version, storage, HA tier, security posture — with no unsafe defaults.

rules.description: The spec must declare platform, engine, engine_version, instance_class, storage_type, storage_size_gb, multi_az, deletion_protection, encryption_at_rest, backup_retention_days, and ha_tier. Missing any field makes the spec incomplete.
engine_version must map to a PostgreSQL major version >= 12. EOL versions (11 and below) receive no security patches and must not be used.
Any instance with pii: true must have encryption_at_rest: true. Storing plaintext PII violates GDPR Article 25 and HIPAA §164.312.
Any instance with ha_tier: production must have deletion_protection: true. Without it, the entire database can be destroyed with a single API call.
Any instance with ha_tier: production must have multi_az: true. Single-AZ production databases are a single point of failure for availability.
Production instances must have backup_retention_days >= 7. This baseline satisfies most compliance frameworks including SOC2 and PCI-DSS.
If provisioned_iops is declared, storage_type must be io1 or io2. gp2/magnetic are flagged for production use. serverless must not declare provisioned_iops.
